name: Fuzzing & Automated Testing
description: Fuzzing techniques, coverage-guided testing, and bug-finding pipelines.

ccs.narrative:
Fuzzing at CCS has progressed from methodology critique to domain-specific fuzzers and finally to AI-augmented test generation. The watershed paper was Evaluating Fuzz Testing (CCS 2018), which exposed that prior fuzzer comparisons lacked statistical rigor and established evaluation standards the community adopted broadly. Hawkeye: Towards a Desired Directed Grey-box Fuzzer (CCS 2018) answered the need for targeted fuzzing toward specific vulnerability sites.

The 2019-2020 period diversified fuzzing targets. Matryoshka: Fuzzing Deeply Nested Branches (CCS 2019) solved the constraint-depth problem using taint analysis and ODE-based path prioritization. Learning to Fuzz from Symbolic Execution with Application to Smart Contracts (CCS 2019) demonstrated how learned fuzzing policies can transfer symbolic execution insights to coverage-guided fuzzers. SQUIRREL (CCS 2020) applied language-aware feedback to fuzz DBMS parsers, and Snipuzz (CCS 2021) tackled black-box IoT firmware without source code.

The 2022 era produced infrastructure and specialization. LibAFL: A Framework to Build Modular and Reusable Fuzzers (CCS 2022) gave researchers a composable toolkit for building custom fuzzing pipelines, while DriveFuzz: Discovering Autonomous Driving Bugs through Driving Quality-Guided Fuzzing (CCS 2022) used driving quality metrics as a feedback signal to find AV safety bugs, extending fuzzing from correctness to physical safety.

ndss.narrative:
Fuzzing research at NDSS opened with a strong focus on embedded and IoT targets, a gap left by AFL-era tools designed for desktop programs. IoTFuzzer (NDSS 2018) sidestepped the inaccessibility of closed firmware by driving fuzzing through the companion mobile app, while What You Corrupt Is Not What You Crash (NDSS 2018) diagnosed why standard crash-based oracles fail on microcontrollers and proposed rehosting as a fix.

The 2019–2020 wave introduced techniques that addressed the core limitations of coverage-guided greybox fuzzing. REDQUEEN (NDSS 2019) cracked magic bytes and checksums cheaply through input-to-state correspondence, eliminating the need for expensive symbolic execution in most cases. NAUTILUS (NDSS 2019) used grammars to generate syntactically valid inputs for language interpreters, while Send Hardest Problems My Way (NDSS 2019) improved hybrid fuzzing by probabilistically routing unsolvable paths to a concolic engine. HFL (NDSS 2020) then applied this hybrid philosophy directly to the Linux kernel, discovering critical vulnerabilities previously hidden from kernel fuzzers.

More recently fuzzing has expanded into specialized domains and absorbed ML techniques. Reinforcement Learning-based Hierarchical Seed Scheduling (NDSS 2021) replaced hand-crafted seed selection heuristics with learned policies; FUZZILLI (NDSS 2023) targeted JavaScript JIT compiler internals; and Large Language Model guided Protocol Fuzzing (NDSS 2024) used LLMs to understand protocol specifications and guide input generation, achieving citation counts that reflect the field's excitement about AI-augmented fuzzing. MTZK (NDSS 2025) further extended the target space to zero-knowledge proof compilers, showing that fuzzing now reaches every corner of the modern software stack.

sp.narrative:
IEEE S&P's fuzzing program opened in 2018 with papers targeting the core weakness of coverage-guided greybox fuzzing: bypassing hard constraints. Angora: Efficient Fuzzing by Principled Search (S&P 2018) replaced random mutation with gradient-descent-like byte-level search to solve branch predicates without symbolic execution. CollAFL: Path Sensitive Fuzzing (S&P 2018) fixed hash collisions in AFL's edge bitmap that masked true path coverage, while T-Fuzz: Fuzzing by Program Transformation (S&P 2018) removed sanity-check barriers to exploration entirely.

The 2019 wave pushed toward smarter guidance. NEUZZ: Efficient Fuzzing with Neural Program Smoothing (S&P 2019) used a neural proxy to compute input gradients and steer mutation toward uncovered branches. ProFuzzer: On-the-fly Input Type Probing (S&P 2019) inferred semantic input structure on the fly for more meaningful mutations. Razzer: Finding Kernel Race Bugs through Fuzzing (S&P 2019) extended greybox fuzzing to kernel concurrency by using a hypervisor to schedule thread interleavings, opening a new target class.

From 2020, S&P papers diversified targets and hardened infrastructure. SAVIOR: Towards Bug-Driven Hybrid Testing (S&P 2020) combined coverage fuzzing with concolic execution steered by bug-triggering potential. RetroWrite: Statically Instrumenting COTS Binaries for Fuzzing and Sanitization (S&P 2020) solved feedback-guided fuzzing on stripped binaries without source code. Ijon: Exploring Deep State Spaces via Fuzzing (S&P 2020) introduced human-readable annotations to express exploration goals that pure coverage cannot capture.

Later years saw fuzzing colonize new domains: DifuzzRTL: Differential Fuzz Testing to Find CPU Bugs (S&P 2021) brought differential fuzzing to hardware RTL designs, BEACON: Directed Grey-Box Fuzzing with Provable Path Pruning (S&P 2022) provided provably sound pruning for directed fuzzing, and by 2023-2024 papers combined fuzzing with LLM-guided mutation and applied it to trusted applications and protocol stacks.

uss.narrative:
The earliest works in this set tackle a core limitation of plain greybox fuzzing: getting past hard, structured input checks. QSYM: A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing (USENIX 2018) made hybrid fuzzing practical by building a fast concolic engine to solve the branch constraints that coverage-guided fuzzers stall on, while MoonShine (USENIX 2018) attacked the same "where do good seeds come from" problem for OS kernel fuzzers via trace distillation. Alongside these, the community began pushing fuzzing into domains that resist naive byte mutation — embedded firmware in Inception (USENIX 2018) — setting up two enduring themes: smarter input reasoning, and re-hosting hard-to-run targets.

The 2019-2020 wave is dominated by two breakthroughs. First, making the fuzzer itself smarter about program semantics: GRIMOIRE (USENIX 2019) synthesizes input structure on the fly, GREYONE (USENIX 2020) uses data-flow/taint to learn which input bytes matter, EcoFuzz (USENIX 2020) reframes seed scheduling as a multi-armed bandit problem, and Montage (USENIX 2020) brings neural language models to JavaScript-engine fuzzing. FuzzGen (USENIX 2020) automated the tedious step of writing fuzz harnesses for libraries. Second, an explosion of domain-specific fuzzing infrastructure: FIRM-AFL (USENIX 2019) and HALucinator (USENIX 2020) made IoT firmware fuzzable through augmented emulation and abstraction-layer re-hosting, while USBFuzz (USENIX 2020) and Frankenstein (USENIX 2020) reached into USB drivers and Bluetooth stacks. RVFuzzer (USENIX 2019) extended the idea to robotic-vehicle control logic, and AURORA (USENIX 2020) addressed the downstream pipeline problem of automatically explaining the many crashes fuzzers produce.

By 2021-2022 the field matured along three fronts. Directed and feedback-rich fuzzing sharpened with Constraint-guided Directed Greybox Fuzzing (USENIX 2021), FuzzGuard's deep-learning input filtering (USENIX 2020), and The Use of Likely Invariants as Feedback for Fuzzers (USENIX 2021). Learning-based control matured with SyzVegas (USENIX 2021), which used reinforcement learning to tune kernel fuzzing decisions. Infrastructure kept advancing: Nyx (USENIX 2021) enabled hypervisor fuzzing with fast snapshots, Breaking Through Binaries (USENIX 2021) brought compiler-quality instrumentation to binary-only targets, and Fuzzware (USENIX 2022) refined firmware fuzzing with precise MMIO modeling. Stateful Greybox Fuzzing (USENIX 2022) and earlier protocol state fuzzing work tackled reactive, stateful systems, and TheHuzz (USENIX 2022) pushed fuzzing down to processor instruction verification.

Most recently the targets themselves have shifted: LLM-Fuzzer (USENIX 2024) repurposes the fuzzing mindset to scale assessment of large-language-model jailbreaks, signaling that the area's core ideas — coverage-style feedback, automated mutation, and bug-finding pipelines — are now being applied well beyond traditional software, even to AI systems.

top4.narrative:
In 2018 the field was busy turning the raw idea of fuzzing into something rigorous and steerable. A foundational concern was simply doing the science right: "Evaluating Fuzz Testing" (CCS 2018) showed that many published gains evaporated under careful statistical comparison, setting evaluation norms the whole community would lean on. Alongside this, papers attacked the core weakness of random mutation — getting past hard checks in the code. "Angora: Efficient Fuzzing by Principled Search" (S&P 2018) used taint and gradient-style search to solve input constraints, "QSYM" (USENIX 2018) made concolic execution fast enough to pair with a fuzzer in true hybrid mode, and "T-Fuzz" (S&P 2018) simply transformed away the checks blocking coverage. Others refined coverage itself ("CollAFL", S&P 2018) or aimed fuzzing at specific targets ("Hawkeye", CCS 2018), while a parallel thread pushed fuzzing onto hard-to-reach platforms like IoT apps ("IoTFuzzer", NDSS 2018), embedded firmware ("What You Corrupt Is Not What You Crash", NDSS 2018), and OS kernels ("MoonShine", USENIX 2018).

2019 brought sharper tricks for the constraint and structure problems. "REDQUEEN" (NDSS 2019) exploited input-to-state correspondence to crack magic bytes and checksums almost for free, a result so cheap and effective it reshaped later fuzzers. For programs needing highly structured input, grammar-aware generation took hold with "NAUTILUS" (NDSS 2019) and, for JavaScript engines, "CodeAlchemist" (NDSS 2019). Machine learning entered seriously through "NEUZZ" (S&P 2019), which approximated program behavior with a neural net to guide mutation. The hybrid-fuzzing line matured with smarter scheduling ("Send Hardest Problems My Way", NDSS 2019), and fuzzing reached new bug classes and domains — kernel data races ("Razzer", S&P 2019) and IoT firmware at speed ("FIRM-AFL", USENIX 2019) — while "Full-Speed Fuzzing" (S&P 2019) cut instrumentation overhead and "ProFuzzer" (S&P 2019) probed input types on the fly.

By 2020 the work was about being smarter per execution and reaching deeper state. Data-flow guidance ("GREYONE", USENIX 2020) and bug-driven hybrid testing ("SAVIOR", S&P 2020) prioritized effort where bugs were likely; "Ijon" (S&P 2020) let humans annotate programs to escape deep state-space traps. Tooling broadened the reach of fuzzing: "RetroWrite" (S&P 2020) instrumented stripped binaries, "FuzzGen" (USENIX 2020) auto-generated library fuzzers, and firmware re-hosting ("HALucinator", USENIX 2020) plus kernel hybrid fuzzing ("HFL", NDSS 2020) opened systems software. Domain-specific validity feedback appeared for databases ("SQUIRREL", CCS 2020), efficiency was framed as a bandit problem ("EcoFuzz", USENIX 2020), and filesystem races got dedicated fuzzers ("Krace", S&P 2020).

The most recent stretch consolidates and specializes. Hardware joined the party with differential RTL fuzzing ("DifuzzRTL", S&P 2021), directed fuzzing gained provable guarantees ("BEACON", S&P 2022), and IoT firmware testing went black-box via message inference ("Snipuzz", CCS 2021). Crucially, "LibAFL" (CCS 2022) turned the field's accumulated tricks into a modular, reusable framework rather than one-off forks. Most recently, large language models entered as a generator of structured inputs, with "Large Language Model guided Protocol Fuzzing" (NDSS 2024) using an LLM to fuzz protocols that lack any machine-readable specification — signaling where the area is heading next.
